module_title: Types of Mortgages, Lease Mechanics, and Gift Registration
introduction: This intermediate tier drives into the specific mechanics of these transfers. It breaks down the 6 types of Mortgages, how Leases are created and terminated, and the strict procedural rules for making a Gift legally valid.

core_concepts.title: The 6 Types of Mortgages (Section 58)
core_concepts.description:
1. Simple Mortgage: No possession given. Mortgagor binds himself personally to pay. If he fails, the mortgagee has the right to cause the property to be sold via court.
2. Mortgage by Conditional Sale: Ostensible sale. 'I sell you this house, but if I repay the loan by December, the sale becomes void. If I fail, the sale becomes absolute.'
3. Usufructuary Mortgage: Possession is delivered to the mortgagee. The mortgagee retains possession and receives the rents/profits from the property until the loan is repaid.
4. English Mortgage: Absolute transfer of property to the mortgagee, with a binding condition that it will be re-transferred upon repayment.
5. Mortgage by Deposit of Title Deeds (Equitable Mortgage): Delivering the original property documents to the creditor. (Very common in bank loans).
6. Anomalous Mortgage: A mortgage that doesn't fit into the above 5 categories (often a mix).

core_concepts.title: Creation and Termination of Leases
core_concepts.description:
- Creation (Sec 107): A lease of immovable property from year-to-year, or for any term exceeding one year, can be made ONLY by a registered instrument.
- Determination/Termination (Sec 111): A lease ends by: (1) Efflux of time (period expires), (2) Implied surrender (tenant accepts a new lease before the old one ends), (3) Forfeiture (tenant breaks a strict condition, like not paying rent, and landlord gives notice), (4) Merger (tenant buys the house, so the lease merges into ownership).

core_concepts.title: Formalities of a Gift (Section 123)
core_concepts.description:
The law is extremely strict regarding Gifts to prevent fraud.
- Immovable Property: Must ALWAYS be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor, and attested by at least two witnesses. (Even if the property is worth ₹10, registration is mandatory).
- Movable Property: Can be effected either by a registered instrument OR by physical delivery of the property.

core_concepts.title: Onerous Gifts & Universal Donee
core_concepts.description:
- Onerous Gift (Sec 127): A gift of a single thing containing both benefits and burdens (e.g., heavily taxed/mortgaged property). The donee must accept it fully or reject it fully; cannot accept the benefit and reject the burden.
- Universal Donee (Sec 128): A person who is gifted the *entire* property of the donor. The universal donee becomes personally liable for all the debts and liabilities of the donor at the time of the gift (up to the value of the gifted property).

important_entities.name: Notice to Quit (Section 106)
important_entities.significance: If a lease doesn't have a fixed end date (periodic), it must be terminated by notice. For Agricultural/Manufacturing leases: 6 months' notice expiring with the year of tenancy. For any other lease (like residential): 15 days' notice expiring with the month of tenancy.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If A writes a registered gift deed transferring his house to B. Before B can accept the gift, A dies. Is the gift valid? **NO**. Section 122 states the gift is void if the donor dies before acceptance. What if B dies before acceptance? Also **Void**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: S C U E D A (Simple, Conditional, Usufructuary, English, Deposit, Anomalous)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use SCUEDA to list all 6 types under Section 58.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary question asks 'In which type of mortgage is possession of the property delivered to the mortgagee to enjoy the rents and profits?', select **Usufructuary Mortgage**.
